scope: Determine whether a complete, independently validated ICC profile can strengthen one public rendering-intent consumer regression. This is a fixture/assertion-quality review, not ICC implementation certification.

source.icc_primary: doc/ICC.1-2022-05.pdf (local ICC.1:2022 primary source; extracted text in this scratch directory for locator searches)

locators.rule: Version bytes encode v4.4.0.0 as 04400000h; reserved bytes zero.
Non-DeviceLink profiles require profileDescription, copyright, and mediaWhitePoint tags.
Monochrome Display profile requires grayTRC; A2B0/1/2 and B2A0/1/2 may be included and use Table 25 semantics.
For Display profiles, A2B0 is perceptual, A2B1 colorimetric, and A2B2 saturation; the matrix/GrayTRC path is colorimetric.
A2B tags define device/encoding-to-PCS transforms; permitted types include lut16Type.
Monochrome Display required tags: profileDescription, grayTRC, mediaWhitePoint, copyright; chromaticAdaptation only when actual adopted white differs from PCS white.

source.pdf_primary: doc/ISO_32000-2_sponsored_EC3.pdf; existing effective §8.6.5.8 color-space rendering-intent and §8.6.5.3 ICCBased sources reviewed in sibling shards; current draft tests a public PDF content stream through interpretation and CPU rasterization.
source.effective_rule_limit: ICC Table 25 provides profile-tag intent mapping. The exact screen RGB pixels are an implementation regression oracle, not values mandated by PDF or ICC.

profile.header: ICC.1 v4.4; mntr / GRAY / XYZ; valid 128-byte header; ProfileID zero indicates not calculated; PCS/media white D50; reserved fields zero.
profile.optional_tag: A2B0/A2B1/A2B2 are permitted for monochrome Display; each is a complete lut16Type mft2 transform. A2B1 midpoint follows the PCS D50 neutral axis. Tag directory entries are unique, aligned, and in-bounds.
profile.validator: ICC iccDEV 2.3.2.5 Python API validate_profile_file; status ValidationStatus.OK, empty report.
profile.fixture_status: Independent ICC-format validation completed. This does not constitute validation by a second ICC implementation or a PDF conformance validator.

consumer_draft.shape: Exact-xref PDF 2.0 with valid ICCBased /N 1 Gray resource, embedded profile, and actual fill content using Perceptual/RelativeColorimetric/Saturation intent; requires complete interpretation and no recovery; reads a painted CPU raster pixel.
consumer_draft.oracle: derive_expected.py extracts the quantized middle mft2 knots from the generated bytes, applies the fixed D50 XYZ-to-sRGB matrix and IEC sRGB transfer curve, then rounds to bytes. These expected display pixels are renderer-specific. The test has not been compiled/run by this reviewer.

comparison.existing: crates/pdf-model/tests/icc_paint_context.rs builds deliberately small custom profiles with distinct A2B tables and strong consumer assertions; the headers omit parts required for complete-profile validity. That is useful implementation-unit coverage, but the fixtures cannot themselves establish a conforming ICC-profile input path.
comparison.prior_validated_profile: Sibling B25 fixture in scratchpad/r2038/spec-audit/colour_spaces_current/drafts/icc2_v5_lab_mpe.icc (see accompanying generator/checker); it is a valid ICC.2 v5 Lab candidate with mpet A2B/B2A tables and was independently accepted by the same ICC iccDEV 2.3.2.5 validator. It is suited to unsupported-profile fallback tests, while the new ICC.1 profile directly exercises implemented lut16 A2B intent selection.
comparison.assessment: A separate valid-profile public consumer control is justified. Replacing the existing focused synthetic-profile suite is not justified; keep the minimal fixtures for targeted numeric cases and use this complete ICC.1 profile to close only the profile-validity gap.

execution: Generator, expected-value derivation, ICCDEV validation run locally. No Cargo or Rust test execution; public draft awaits parent integration/run.
